definition.description: Whether carboplatin was administered to the patient.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract 'Yes' if the patient record contains any evidence of carboplatin administration, prescription, or mention in a treatment regimen; otherwise, extract 'No'.
definition.missing_value_rule: Absent or ambiguous documentation is represented as 'No'.
definition.name: carboplatin_administered

definition.description: Presence of cataracts at the time of pretreatment assessment.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient is documented to have cataracts in the pretreatment record, typically found in the comorbidities section or HEENT physical examination findings.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if cataracts are not mentioned or documentation is ambiguous.
definition.name: cataracts

definition.description: Presence of abnormal contrast enhancement in the cavernous sinuses.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether post-contrast imaging (e.g., gadolinium-enhanced T1-weighted MRI) indicates abnormal enhancement of the cavernous sinuses. Report 'Present' if abnormal enhancement is identified and 'Absent' if the report explicitly states 'no abnormal enhancement' or describes the cavernous sinuses as 'unremarkable'.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the cavernous sinuses are not mentioned or if the imaging was performed without contrast.
definition.name: cavernous_sinus_enhancement

definition.description: The mutation status of the CDKN2A gene, specifically whether a homozygous deletion or loss is present in the tumor tissue.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the CDKN2A status from Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) or molecular profiling reports. Identify 'homozygous deletion', 'homozygous loss', or 'loss' as the mutation status. If the gene is listed as not mutated, not altered, or is absent from the genomic findings table while other genes are listed, it should be extracted as 'wild-type'.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if molecular testing for CDKN2A was not performed or is not documented in the patient record.
definition.name: cdkn2a_mutation_status

definition.description: Blood concentration of Carcinoembryonic Antigen (CEA), a tumor marker used for monitoring non-small cell lung cancer.
definition.measurement_definition: The numeric value of the CEA level extracted from laboratory tumor marker results in the pretreatment record.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the CEA level is not documented or the value is ambiguous.
definition.name: cea_level

definition.description: Patient use of the antibiotic cefepime
definition.measurement_definition: Identify if the patient record explicitly mentions the administration or prescription of cefepime.
definition.missing_value_rule: Absent or ambiguous documentation is represented as 'No'.
definition.name: cefepime_use

definition.description: Qualitative assessment of the MRI signal intensity of the cerebellar hemispheres.
definition.measurement_definition: From the neuroimaging report (specifically the posterior fossa or brain parenchyma sections), extract whether the signal intensity of the cerebellar hemispheres is described as normal or abnormal.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the cerebellar hemisphere signal is not mentioned or is undocumented.
definition.name: cerebellar_hemisphere_signal

definition.description: The qualitative assessment of the size of the cerebellar hemispheres.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the qualitative description of the cerebellar hemisphere size (e.g., normal, enlarged, atrophic, small) from the posterior fossa or parenchyma section of the neuroimaging report.
definition.missing_value_rule: If the size of the cerebellar hemispheres is not explicitly mentioned or is ambiguous, the value should be represented as null.
definition.name: cerebellar_hemisphere_size

definition.description: Presence of white matter lesions within the cerebellum.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the presence or absence of cerebellar white matter lesions from pretreatment radiology or clinical reports.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if documentation is missing or ambiguous.
definition.name: cerebellar_white_matter_lesion_presence

definition.description: Qualitative assessment of the signal intensity of the cerebral gray matter on MRI.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the descriptive term used to characterize the signal intensity of the cerebral hemispheric gray matter (e.g., 'normal', 'increased', 'decreased', 'hyperintense', 'hypointense'). Map 'hyperintense' to 'increased' and 'hypointense' to 'decreased'.
definition.missing_value_rule: If signal intensity for the cerebral gray matter is not mentioned or is ambiguous, represent as missing.
definition.name: cerebral_gray_matter_signal_intensity

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
